findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves. It answers "what is this" and "why does it matter" before anything else.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The page explains why someone who came for Athena is reading about a different project. Without this, the title "Athena explains how firstmate handles work" would be confusing, because it names firstmate before saying what firstmate is.
findings.source: "Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it with every statement traced to a claim"

findings.text: The first section after the intro is an error message. The lede promises models, verdict and cost, but the one place meant to show them is empty, so a newcomer sees something broken before any real content.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: The next steps are concrete: prerequisites, the clone command, ./setup.sh, and a first command to try. A newcomer knows what to do next, and the lede links straight to this section.
findings.source: Next steps: "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm" ... "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: This link is in the intro, but a first-time visitor is not the owner. It is unclear whether it is meant for them, which adds noise at the top of the page.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The middle of the page is long and dense: twelve transition cards, exit codes 75 and 1, and 45 claims. That depth suits someone checking firstmate's internals. A newcomer judging Athena is likely to skim it, and transition ids like t1 are used here before the Transitions section defines them.
findings.source: Counters: "places-held, changed by transitions t1, t3, t4, t9, t11"

findings.text: Several glossary entries say the term is undefined instead of explaining it. This is honest, but it leaves the reader without a working meaning for words the page uses.
findings.source: Glossary: "The firstmate source does not define a durable record." (similar entries for endpoint, heartbeat, wake, captain call)

findings.text: The last sections describe how the study was produced and where its data is stored. That is useful for auditing but of little use to a newcomer, and the note that a first reading missed paths may make them trust it less without explaining why it matters.
findings.source: Limits of this study, f3: "A first reading of the pinned tree missed these paths"; About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/"
